title: A Shared Knowledge Base
alt: You and several agent harnesses read and update a shared knowledge base containing activity and working state, personal context, and knowledge and reference material. Agents also access external sources through tools, while notes can link to those sources.

title: From a Knowledge Base to a Workspace
alt: A shared agent workspace contains a knowledge base plus instructions and maps, skills and resources, and tool connections, used together across harnesses.

title: The Knowledge Lifecycle
alt: A task leads through a combined retrieval and context assembly step, then agent work. A two-way arrow connects retrieval with the knowledge base for lookups and returned information. Useful information is captured, and routine updates go directly to writeback. Changes needing review take a separate path before writeback. Temporary responses stay outside the knowledge base.

title: Examples of Summarized Views
alt: Three examples of summarized views, each shown as a horizontal sequence. Across time: daily notes to weekly reviews to a monthly summary. Across a project: meeting notes and work logs to decision summaries to a project overview. Across a topic: notes on individual sources to summaries of related ideas to a topic overview. Each view keeps links to its supporting material.

title: Access and Synchronization Models
alt: Three access and synchronization models side by side. Central access connects two devices to a shared service holding the knowledge base. Server-mediated synchronization exchanges changes between a server copy and local copies on each device. Peer-to-peer synchronization exchanges changes among devices that each hold a local copy. Examples include Notion for central access; iCloud, Google Drive, Dropbox, and Obsidian Sync for server-mediated synchronization; and Syncthing for peer-to-peer synchronization.

title: Personal Agents, from Hobby Project to Mainstream
alt: A timeline from November 2025 to September 2026. Open-source milestones: OpenClaw, Mac minis selling out, Hermes Agent, and OpenClaw 2.0. Large-company milestones: OpenClaw's creator joining OpenAI, Google Gemini Spark, Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots, and Instinct at a $10B valuation.

title: From Asking Questions to Getting Things Done
alt: A spectrum from asking to getting things done. Asking examples: explain this lease clause, rewrite my email, plan a weekend in Victoria. Getting-things-done examples: book the ferry and hotel, cancel my gym membership, sit through the insurance call. Most ChatGPT use sits at the asking end. Getting things done involves three steps: pick the task, grant access, and live with the result.

title: Where Your Data Lives
alt: A comparison of where a personal agent's data lives. On your machine (OpenClaw, Hermes): memory is plain files on a machine you own, logins and keys stay on your machine, you vet every skill and keep the machine locked down, and you take your files to the next agent. In their cloud (Muse, Dots, Gemini Spark): memory is stored on the company's servers, email, calendar, and payments are linked to their agent, the company runs security with isolated VMs and approval checks, and switching means rebuilding what the agent knew about you.
